t: Based at Palembang in Sumatra, Srivijaya was a sea power that ruled the Strait of Malacca from the 7th to the 13th century.
It grew rich by taxing China-India shipping and became a renowned centre of Buddhist learning, spreading Old Malay across the region.
Chola raids, Javanese rivals, direct Chinese shipping and the spread of Islam wore it down until Temasek and Malacca took its role.
dyk: The Chinese pilgrim Yijing, who stopped there in 671, found over a thousand Buddhist monks and advised Chinese monks to study in Srivijaya before going to India.
